It really depends on taste. One would argue tiling DE is the best for workflow. I will stick with gnome 3.x because of the overview of windows, and the easy application starter.

Cinnamon. Less context switching which human brains are really bad at. Really bad at.

Running a program shouldn't involve entering a different context visually.

It also does the same thing for changing open applications. It also gives you constant overview of what is open.

It's funny how people like nerdtree for vim but they don't want to see a list of open applications. The truth, people do want to see a list of open applications. It has to do with something we all should be familiar with "branch misses." When you say to yourself I want to do blank, and before you even move a mouse you plan out what you are doing instictually inside your head. Well if it's ambiguous whether you are switching to an open application or launching it then you have to do recall. This ambiguousness in planning increases stress (almost the source of all stress). Of course it's easily remedyable by opening your application menu but that involves an action but that means that you have to think about what you are going to do, recognize that you don't have enough information to make a decision, contemplate what you need to do to get that information, perform that action, use that information to go back into planning mode and resolve the "branch" then execute it.

Or you could just visually see you have it open in one glance and open it.

All of this breaks mental focus. A few pixels are worth maintained context. Now if all you want to do is browse the internet and you want maximum real estate then those 24 pixels on the bottom may be worth it to you.
